candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Hymns on the Nativity
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Hymns on the Nativity I.18; cp. Hymns on the Crucifixion I.2-3 (NPNF S2 V13, Gwynn/Schaff trans., Oxford 1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Hymns on the Nativity (c. 365 AD)

The bush that burns yet is not consumed is, for Ephrem, the first canonical type of the Theotokos: the holy fire of divinity dwelling within the bush of Mary's flesh without consuming it. Tewahedo iconography seats the burning bush among its earliest Marian types, and the bush is a regular figure in Marian hymnody: 'the bush that bore the fire and was not burned.'
candidates.reviewer_notes: Curated PD interpretive summary representing the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition's reading via Ephrem the Syrian, Hymns on the Nativity. Verify the summary still reflects the source's argument before promoting; substitute a verbatim quote from the NPNF / Charles dump where available, and where applicable cross-check the Andəmta homiletic tradition for resonance.

candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Exodus
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Exodus III.2 (NPNF S2 V13, Gwynn/Schaff trans., Oxford 1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Exodus (c. 360 AD)

'Loose thy shoe from off thy foot, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground' — Ephrem hears in this not only Moses' singular calling but the rule for entering the sanctuary, that what carries the dust of the world is removed before standing where God has descended. Tewahedo carries this as the canonical warrant for entering the Beta Maryam barefoot, a practice preserved in every Tewahedo church to this day.

candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Sermo de Domino Nostro
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Sermo de Domino Nostro 4-5 (NPNF S2 V13). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Sermo de Domino Nostro (c. 363 AD)

'I AM THAT I AM' is, for Ephrem, the divine Name revealed in advance of the Incarnation as the very ground on which the Word may later say 'Before Abraham was, I am' (Jn 8:58). The Name is not given to Moses as a label but as a confession: God reveals himself as the eternal subsisting One whose being underwrites every act of deliverance. Tewahedo reads Ex 3:14 and Jn 8:58 as a single canonical disclosure.

Ephrem the Syrian Hymns on the Nativity (c. 365 AD)

The bush that burns yet is not consumed is, for Ephrem, the first canonical type of the Theotokos: the holy fire of divinity dwelling within the bush of Mary's flesh without consuming it. Tewahedo iconography seats the burning bush among its earliest Marian types, and the bush is a regular figure in Marian hymnody: 'the bush that bore the fire and was not burned.'

Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Exodus (c. 360 AD)

'Loose thy shoe from off thy foot, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground' — Ephrem hears in this not only Moses' singular calling but the rule for entering the sanctuary, that what carries the dust of the world is removed before standing where God has descended. Tewahedo carries this as the canonical warrant for entering the Beta Maryam barefoot, a practice preserved in every Tewahedo church to this day.

Ephrem the Syrian Sermo de Domino Nostro (c. 363 AD)

'I AM THAT I AM' is, for Ephrem, the divine Name revealed in advance of the Incarnation as the very ground on which the Word may later say 'Before Abraham was, I am' (Jn 8:58). The Name is not given to Moses as a label but as a confession: God reveals himself as the eternal subsisting One whose being underwrites every act of deliverance. Tewahedo reads Ex 3:14 and Jn 8:58 as a single canonical disclosure.

Athanasius of Alexandria De Decretis Nicaenae Synodi §22 (c. 350 AD)

'And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM... Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you' — Athanasius marks the LXX egō eimi ho ōn (I-AM the-Being-One) as the foundational name-of-God revelation that the Word inherits and reveals in Jn 8:58 (prin Abraam genesthai egō eimi — 'before Abraham was, I am'). The divine egō-eimi is unshareable with any creature; that the incarnate-Word uses it self-referentially at Jn 6:35 + 8:12 + 10:7 + 10:11 + 11:25 + 14:6 + 15:1 (the seven Johannine I-AM sayings) is therefore self-identification with the Burning-Bush God.
